messages:
monitoring-bot: ALERT: SLO burn detected for hosted-inference API (ingress.gateway) — 5m p99 latency 2.3s, error rate (5xx) 4.8% (SLO threshold 1%). Alert ID: A-87921 :rotating_light:
support-ops: Customer ticket #C-12789 reporting timeouts and 502s across multiple regions. They reported 20% of requests failing for the last 12m. Already escalated.
ranjit: saw that. dashboards show a sharp spike starting ~2412000600. Grafana link: https://grafana.internal/graph?orgId=1&panelId=34 (ingress p99 + 5xx).
maria: on it. Can someone share a sample request/trace id from the ticket?
support-ops: here's the customer's sample request id: req_3f2a9b7c. They included this in logs and said curl to hosted endpoint returned 502 after ~1.8s.
oles: checking traces for req_3f2a9b7c — trace not found in Jaeger. We have a gap between ingress and authz traces around that time. Possibly the request never reached downstream service instrumentation.
kevin: billing-bot reported a billing backend error around same timeframe: "billing-queue: 5xx rate from auth-service". billing-bot: "ERR_QUEUE_OVERFLOW 503 at 2412000675".
oncall-sre: putting a small mitigation: increasing ingress proxy upstream timeout from 1.5s -> 3s for the next 15m to reduce immediate user-facing 502s. Will roll back after.
ranjit: good call. But we need root cause. My hunch: authz service experiencing intermittent thrash due to a recent deploy or token validation calls to billing KMS causing stalls.
maria: pulling logs from ingress for trace window. Query (clickhouse):
```
select timestamp, request_id, status_code, latency_ms, upstream from ingress_logs where timestamp between 2412000500 and 2412000800 and request_id = 'req_3f2a9b7c'
```
Result: ingress returned 502 with upstream "authz" and latency ~1800ms.
oles: trying to reproduce locally with the same header set (customer uses a long cookie). Repro: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "Cookie: session=...long..." https://api.hosted.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
I get a 502 after ~1.7s when upstream authz takes a long time.
kevin: check authz metrics. There are a couple of pods with CPU spikes and a small GC pause pattern. Also seeing an unusual increase in token validation latency hitting the KMS — RPC latencies to kms-east are 600-900ms.
support-ops: customer says they started seeing this after their project switched billing plans (auto-upgrade) earlier today. Could be an authz path that validates billing entitlements synchronously.
ranjit: yep, entitlements call is sync in authz. If KMS or billing cache goes slow, downstream requests pile up. Need to short-circuit on cache miss or add async validation.
maria: creating queries to correlate KMS latency to ingress 5xx. Clickhouse query attached. Also adding an alert for KMS RPC > 300ms for 5m.
oles: also note tracing gap — ingress emits trace id but authz side didn't pick it up for many requests. Possible sampling misconfiguration or dropped headers on authz ingress.
kevin: reproduced header drop locally when request size > 4KB and our internal LB truncates headers. The customer's cookie might be large and causing header truncation which then breaks tracing and causes authz to fall back to sync validation and block.
oncall-sre: mitigation plan: 1) increase proxy header size limit on LB for 30m; 2) keep upstream timeout bumped; 3) add circuit-breaker on authz to return 429/202 fallback rather than 502 if entitlements backend is slow.
maria: making a quickrun playbook for Support to send to customer: ask them to try with minimal headers (no cookie) to see if it reduces failures. Include curl snippet:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt":"test"}' https://api.hosted.redwood/v1/generate
```
If that reduces errors, it's likely header size issue.
support-ops: sent that to customer. They're trying now.
monitoring-bot: support-ops updated alert A-87921 status -> acknowledged by oncall-sre.
ranjit: I'm opening an incident ticket and assigning owners: authz-service (kevin), network (oles), billing (kevin + billing-bot watch), support (support-ops). Incident link: https://incidents.internal/INC-2024-512
kevin: digging into recent authz deploys — one rolled 30m before spike. Rollback suggestion? The change was a dependency bump that touched KMS client. There are 3 failures in canary logs that match the RPC timeouts to KMS. Rolling back to previous image on two pods to see if it stabilizes.
oles: rolling LB header size and proxy timeout now (will take ~2m). Command: `kubectl patch configmap ingress-proxy --patch '{"data":{"proxy_buffer_size":"16k"}}'` and `kubectl rollout restart ds/ingress-proxy`.
maria: adding temporary Grafana panel to show header size rejections and header-related 5xx.
oncall-sre: rollback initiated for authz canary pods. Watching.
kevin: after rollback, authz RPC latencies dropped from ~700ms -> ~80ms on two pods. Error rate dropped to 0.6% in the past 3m.
maria: ingress 5xx now trending down. p99 latency back to 0.9s. Customer on the ticket reports improved success rate.
support-ops: customer confirmed decreased failures after removing cookie from request. They will follow up with their engineering to reduce cookie size.
ranjit: root cause summary: combination of (1) recent authz deploy with KMS client change that increased RPC tail latency, (2) large request headers from one customer causing header truncation/dropped tracing, (3) synchronous entitlement call blocking authz -> ingress returned 502.
ranjit: action items:
- kevin: open PR to make entitlement check async + add graceful fallback (owner: kevin, ETA 3 days)
- oles: increase default proxy_buffer_size cluster-wide and add test for header size (owner: oles, ETA 1 day)
- maria: add synthetic test hitting authz with large headers and monitor (owner: maria, ETA 2 days)
- support-ops: update customer playbook and notify affected customers (owner: support-ops, ETA immediate)
- billing-bot: add observability hooks to billing/KMS RPCs (owner: billing-bot / billing team, ETA 3 days)
kevin: filing a post-incident runbook entry for authz entitlements and KMS client configuration.
maria: marking alert A-87921 resolved in monitoring after stabilization.
support-ops: closing rollout/TTR ticket as customer confirmed mitigation.
oncall-sre: leaving the temporary timeout/header changes in place for the next 2h, then we'll revert to safer defaults once we've verified synthetic tests.
ranjit: thanks everyone. Good cross-team coordination. I'll draft a short postmortem and link back to INC-2024-512.
monitoring-bot: NOTE: please remember to add the incident tag `trace-gap` when creating the postmortem.
